findings.text: The instruction pointer probe dispatcher looks up the probe registered at the faulting address and reports an error when none exists. When a probe is already active it delegates to nested handling, otherwise it marks the new probe current with active status, invokes its pre callback when present, and either arms single stepping on absent or zero result or clears the current probe on nonzero result.

Probe execution moves from active on first hit to single step armed, then to single step done before completion, with a distinct reenter value while a nested probe runs. Nested entry saves outer probe identity status and interrupt flags, and nested completion restores them without invoking outer post processing.

Arming single step depends on whether an out of line slot exists. With a slot the handler preserves interrupt flags and redirects execution to that slot, without a slot it runs an architecture simulator that optionally calls a decoder callback with opcode address and register state then performs common post handling.

Single step entry records the masked interrupt bits from saved processor state and then sets those mask bits, while single step exit clears the mask bits and reinstates the recorded value. Nested probes stash the outer recorded value before overwriting and restore it on unwind so the outer exit restores the original mask.

Only one nesting level is recoverable. Hits arriving while active or during single step preparation or completion increment a missed counter and arm a nested step, a hit while already in reenter state logs and triggers a fatal trap, and any unexpected status warns and signals failure.

The single step completion trap succeeds only when a probe is running, its status indicates armed step or reenter, and the fault address equals just past the first out of line word. On success it restores interrupt flags and runs common post handling, otherwise it reports not owned.

Common post handling restores the faulting address from a saved restore field when nonzero, returns early after reinstating outer state for nested completions, otherwise marks step done, invokes the post callback when present, and clears the current probe.

The return probe trap validates that the program counter equals the shared trampoline symbol and reports not owned otherwise. On match it replaces the program counter with the result of the generic trampoline resolver supplied with registers and the register at index twenty nine.

The bug trap dispatcher classifies the fault address through a generic reporter. Fatal class terminates, warning class continues, unknown class reports not owned, and survivors advance past one fixed width instruction and report handled.

The control flow trap extracts target and type values from registers selected by fields decoded from the syndrome value, then dispatches through a generic failure reporter with fatal warning and unknown outcomes matching the bug trap, advancing survivors past one instruction.

The sanitizer trap decodes recover and write flags plus access size from the syndrome, reports the address held in register zero with size direction and program counter, terminates when recovery is not permitted, otherwise skips one instruction and reports handled.
Access size is one shifted left by the syndrome value masked to its size bits.
The undefined behavior trap always terminates with a message derived from the masked syndrome and reports handled.
The reserved fault trap logs the faulting address as a text patching error and always reports not owned.

The user mode breakpoint entry first attempts the uprobe handler when that feature is enabled and the syndrome comment matches its reserved immediate, returning on success, otherwise it delivers a breakpoint trap signal to the user task. The uprobe handler delegates to a pre single step notifier and reports handled only when that notifier claims the event.
The kernel mode breakpoint entry tries the registered kernel break hook chain and returns on success, otherwise it terminates with a BRK fault.

Thirty two bit breakpoint handling notifies with a BKPT label for the direct vector, while the compatibility probe reads one sixteen bit halfword for Thumb or one thirty two bit word for ARM from user program counter, recognizes three encodings including a two halfword Thumb two form with masking of top nibble for ARM, and on match delivers a breakpoint trap signal and reports true.

Kernel single stepping asserts interrupts are disabled. Enabling sets the saved status step bit and the debug control step bit plus the kernel debug monitor, disabling clears control step and monitor, querying returns the control step bit, and rewind and fastforward set or clear only the saved status step bit.

User stepping is tracked by a thread flag. Enabling sets the flag once and sets the saved status step bit in task registers, disabling clears the flag, and reset of user registers sets or clears the saved status step bit according to the flag.

The runtime wrapper preserves frame pointers and callee saved registers plus the platform register, switches to a dedicated runtime stack while recording the task stack, marshals the service target and up to five register arguments, invokes the target, clears the recorded stack on return, restores registers, verifies the platform register is unchanged, and on mismatch restores a shadow stack variant when configured before tail calling a corruption handler. A separate recover entry restores the task stack from the link register, clears the record, and restores callee saved registers.

Memory mapped IO uses device semantics with an encrypted variant for protected regions and decrypted otherwise. Misaligned regions cannot use strict permissions and fall back to executable kernel pages once any misaligned code region was seen else to nonexecutable kernel pages, with the misaligned code observation being sticky. Aligned regions map read only, read execute, read write, or read write execute from combinations of execute never read only and protection attributes and code type.

Mapping creation derives protection then forces page granularity for runtime code and data and additionally for any region misaligned to the operating system page size to avoid block descriptors shared across rounded neighbors, and always marks the new descriptors non global.

The misalignment check is always false when operating system and firmware page sizes match, otherwise it reports true when either the physical base or the byte length derived from page count is not page aligned.
Page table creation for the runtime mapping path serializes the locked table walk under a fixmap mutex held across the whole range update.

The public creator rejects the initial address space, converts a page only request into no block and no contiguous mapping flags, and delegates to an early creator that terminates the system on any failure. The locked worker validates that physical and virtual bases share the same page offset, rounds the range outward to page boundaries, and iterates directory entries advancing the physical base by the covered span.

Each directory level reuses an existing table through a fixmap offset or on missing entry allocates a child table through a caller supplied allocator failing with out of memory on invalid address, zeroes the new table with a barrier ensuring visibility to hardware walks, and links it with table access and unprivileged execute never attributes plus privileged execute never when no execute mappings were requested. After recursing into the next level it warns if a preexisting entry changed unexpectedly and always clears the fixmap.

A one gigabyte block is attempted only on supporting granules when address next and physical base are all block aligned, block mappings are allowed, and the current entry is not already a table. Population failure warns, and any rewrite of an existing block entry is constrained to safe permission only changes.

Global interfaces observed include breakpoint fault handlers for probes single step return probes bugs control flow and sanitizers, user and kernel single step controls, runtime service mapping creation, and page table creation helpers.

Observed probe object carries pre and post callbacks, an out of line instruction pointer and restore address, an optional simulation callback with opcode and address, and a missed counter incremented on nested hits.

Observed per CPU control block carries a status word, a saved interrupt mask, a current probe pointer held per CPU, and a previous record holding outer probe pointer status and saved mask for one nesting level.
Observed register state carries program counter instruction pointer processor state argument and indexed registers and a user view with saved status step control.
Observed firmware descriptor carries physical base page count virtual base attribute flags and memory type used for protection and mapping decisions.
